title: Cutter Gauthier Jersey: Three Hat Tricks in Eight Days
subheadline: His third hat trick in eight days tied the NHL record for one calendar month and pushed Anaheim's winning streak to five.
description: Cutter Gauthier scored his third hat trick of November in a 5-2 win over Pittsburgh on Nov. 8, tying an NHL record. Why his No. 61 Ducks jersey is rising.
searchIntent: Hockey and Ducks fans who heard about Gauthier's third hat trick in eight days want to know what record he tied and which Gauthier jersey to get.
body: Cutter Gauthier is putting his name next to some of the biggest scorers the NHL has seen. He scored three goals and added an assist as the Anaheim Ducks beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-2 at Honda Center on Nov. 8.

It was his third hat trick in eight days. That tied the NHL record for hat tricks in one calendar month, and NHL.com notes he is the first player ever to get three in the first 10 days of a month. Phil Esposito held the old mark of 13 days, set in December 1970.
## Why fans are buying in

When we wrote about Gauthier after his comeback hat trick against Ottawa on Nov. 1, he was a hot young scorer. A week later he is chasing history. He has goals in six straight games, 13 of them in that span, and a point in eight straight.

The company he keeps is the story. Only Corey Perry, Frank Vatrano and Teemu Selanne had three hat tricks in a single season for the Ducks, and Gauthier did it before mid-November. He is also the first American-born player to score hat tricks in back-to-back home games.

The team is rising with him. Anaheim has won five in a row to reach 10-7-1, and it has scored at least five goals in eight straight games, something only seven other teams in NHL history had done, per NHL.com.

He is 22, Philadelphia's fifth overall pick in 2022, and he scored 41 goals for Anaheim last season. In our analysis, a young scorer setting records for a team on a winning streak is the kind of player fans pick up early and keep wearing. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look
Gauthier wears No. 61, a number few stars wear, so his jersey stands out. The banner above shows the Ducks' bright orange home look in several cuts.
## Why this jersey will last

Gauthier is only in his third full NHL season and is already one of the league's most dangerous shooters. subheadline: With Luka Dončić out, Reaves scored a season-high 43 in Detroit and hit the late 3-pointer that sealed the Lakers' fifth straight win.
description: Austin Reaves scored 43 as the Lakers beat Detroit 121-116 on Nov. 8 without Luka Dončić for a fifth straight win. Why his No. 15 Lakers jersey is rising.

body: Austin Reaves took over when the Los Angeles Lakers needed him. With Luka Dončić sitting out with lower back tightness, Reaves scored a season-high 43 points in a 121-116 win over the Detroit Pistons at Little Caesars Arena on Nov. 8.
He made 14 of 27 shots, 4 of 6 from 3-point range and all 11 of his free throws. His off-balance 3-pointer as the shot clock ran down in the final minute put the game away.
## Why fans are buying in
The win was the Lakers' fifth in a row. They are 9-2, first in the Pacific Division, and 2-0 this season without Dončić, who leads the NBA in scoring.
The opponent made it count. Detroit came in at 6-3 and ranked first in the league on defense, per ESPN, and Reaves still scored 43 against it.

There is a story behind the night, too. ESPN notes Detroit planned to take Reaves 42nd in the 2021 draft, but he went undrafted by choice and signed with the Lakers. Five years later, the player who chose Los Angeles is a lead scorer for one of the West's best teams. He averaged 23.3 points and 5.5 assists last season.

Fans love a player who earned his spot. In our analysis, a former undrafted guard carrying a winning Lakers team on the road is the kind of story that turns a fan favorite into a jersey people want. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look

subheadline: Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns in a 44-22 rout of the Chargers as Houston won for the third time in four games.

body: C.J. Stroud looked like Houston's star again. He completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards and five touchdowns as the Texans beat the Los Angeles Chargers 44-22 at SoFi Stadium on Nov. 8.
He spread the scores around, finding Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, Nico Collins and Kayshon Boutte twice, and Houston piled up a season-best 485 yards.
## Why fans are buying in
The timing matters. The Texans started the season 0-4, and this was their third win in four games. A quarterback who turns a season around gives fans a reason to come back to his jersey.

The supporting cast is part of the appeal. Dell's 63-yard touchdown came in only his second game back after a long recovery from a serious knee injury, and Boutte had 125 yards on four catches. The defense added eight sacks.
Stroud has been here before. He was the 2023 Offensive Rookie of the Year, and he opened this season with 216 straight passes without an interception.

Fans have stayed with him through the ups and downs. He ranked No. 20 on the NFLPA's Top 50 player sales list for licensed merchandise from March 1, 2025, to Feb. 28, 2026. That list covers all player products, not jerseys alone. In our analysis, a big day that sparks a comeback season gives that support a fresh push. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look

## Why this jersey will last

At 25, Stroud is still early in his career and is the face of the franchise, with a young core around him that includes Collins and pass rusher Will Anderson Jr., who had two of the eight sacks against Los Angeles.
